voices.note: Samuel the prophet as a youth, whose ruling and derivation R' Elazar's story reports
Eli the priest, Samuel's teacher, as R' Elazar's story reports him
Hannah, Samuel's mother; her words are the verses I Sam 1:26-27

props.gloss_en: Samuel was one who taught halakha in the presence of his teacher
as it is said: 'and they slaughtered the bull and brought the youth to Eli' (I Sam 1:25)
Eli: call a priest -- let him come and slaughter
Samuel: why seek a priest to slaughter? slaughter by a non-priest is valid
Samuel: is it written 'and the priest shall slaughter'? 'and the priests shall offer' is written -- from receiving onward is the priests' mitzva; from here, that slaughter is valid by a non-priest
Eli: and whoever teaches halakha in the presence of his teacher is liable to death
Hannah, crying before Eli: 'I am the woman who stood by you here...' (I Sam 1:26)
Eli: let me punish him, and I will ask for mercy, and He will give you one greater than him
Hannah to Eli: 'for this youth I prayed' (I Sam 1:27)

supports.gloss_en: שנאמר וישחטו את הפר ויביאו את הנער אל עלי -- משום דוישחטו את הפר הביאו הנער אל עלי? because they slaughtered the bull they brought the youth to Eli? (the juxtaposition is explained by the story that follows)
מקבלה ואילך מצות כהונה, מכאן לשחיטה שכשרה בזר -- since the priests' mitzva begins at receiving the blood, slaughter is valid by a non-priest
